title: Deterministic Verification with a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies to the synthetic/emulation partition only. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent-to-configuration translators for network operations (NetOps), offering rapid authoring of device CLI sequences from natural-language intent. However, stochastic generation can produce syntax errors, incorrect ordering, and vendor-specific misforms that threaten operational safety. A common mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes deterministic validators and, when appropriate, bounded repair templates that attempt mechanical fixes before acceptance. Prior surveys and empirical work document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while stressing the continuing need for deterministic validation or human oversight [1],[2].

This study asks a tightly scoped, preregistered question under shared_initial_candidate semantics: when the identical single LLM-generated candidate for each intent is (a) accepted as-is (baseline) versus (b) submitted to a deterministic validator with at most one automated repair (guarded), what is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction on a synthetic/emulation partition? By holding the initial candidate identical across conditions we isolate only the marginal effect attributable to deterministic validation plus the single permitted repair rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. Our principal contributions are (1) a preregistered, paired, artifact-backed measurement of that marginal effect for N = 250 intents using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), (2) full reconciliation of model-call accounting (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1), and (3) public archival pointers to the preregistration and immutable master prompt (see Disclosure).
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical studies document LLM applications for NetOps intent translation and evaluate generate–verify patterns. Evidence shows that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in constrained setups but often require verification or human oversight to catch mechanistic errors [1],[2]. Deterministic network verifiers and model‑checking tools (e.g., header-space analysis, Batfish-style tools) are mature methods for checking forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[4]. Prior generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows (in code and configuration domains) increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects, while deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain difficult to mechanize [5],[6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers but show adaptive adversaries remain an open threat [7].

This work differs in three ways: (i) the confirmatory paired design uses shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate only validator/repair marginal effects; (ii) the run reconciles stage-level provider accounting to show how many model calls were shared versus repair calls; and (iii) the run archives complete validator traces and deterministic reconciliation artifacts so the numeric outcomes and stage mappings are auditable from the evidence bundle.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (SHA-256: 7a984dbf...) as a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration fixed the one-repair policy, exclusion rules, an exact paired test (McNemar), and a paired-bootstrap CI procedure (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistration artifact is archived and referenced in the Disclosure.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (explicit). Under the registered semantics exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent; that identical candidate was used for both episodes (baseline and guarded). No independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. Provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation artifact) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, which reconciles to 250 shared initial generations plus one repair-stage call.

Task generation, constraints, and partitions. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercise common workflow constraints (make-before-break, paired-link MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns) and protect certain interfaces. The preregistration defined three partitions (emulation/synthetic, community, production-like); the confirmatory execution reported here covers the synthetic/emulation partition only.

Model invocation, validator, and repair policy. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Each intent received one shared initial generation. The guarded pipeline submitted that candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: CLI parsing, command counting, required_sequence ordering checks, workflow-constraint checks, and a final_state snapshot comparison to the task-encoded expected_final_state. If the validator returned valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair constrained to syntactic and ordering fixes (reorder commands to match required_sequence, split multi-command lines, correct token ordering) and re-submitted the repaired candidate once. No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted in the confirmatory run.

Inclusion/exclusion and contamination. Exclusions (pre-registered) remove outputs that fail vendor-parsers in a way that prevents deterministic verification or contain credential-like tokens or denylist matches. Contamination detectors flag embedded instruction-like tokens; flagged episodes would be excluded from primary analysis. In this run no confirmatory episodes were excluded or flagged: complete_pair_count = 250 and contamination_summary is empty.

Analysis. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: exact two-sided McNemar for paired counts and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Sensitivity analyses for missingness and contamination were preregistered but not required for the confirmatory partition because no episodes were excluded.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. Execution completed planned_episode_count = 500 (250 pairs × 2 episodes) with completed_episode_count = 500, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}). No episodes were flagged for contamination and no preregistered exclusions were applied.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the one exercised repair call; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value (discordant counts n10 = 1, n01 = 0) = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0–1.2 percentage points). These analysis artifacts (paired contingency table, condition summary, bootstrap parameters) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.

Representative validator diagnostics. Validator traces for passed episodes report parsed_command_count and required_command_count matching the task payload's required_sequence. Example: task-000003 (hard difficulty) shows parsed_command_count = 6 and required_command_count = 6 and valid = true for both baseline and guarded episodes. Representative scoring artifacts and raw responses are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near-null marginal effect. In the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting deterministic validation plus a single automated repair on identical gpt-5-mini candidates was small: initial candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the only failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the maximum verifier-detected improvement under the study conditions.

Why the marginal effect was small. Artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents, explicit required_sequences, and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced syntactically consistent, well-ordered command sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, snapshot match) and does not measure broader live-protocol behavioral correctness.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline pass ≈ 0.90 to power detection of a 15 percentage-point effect with ~80% power and motivated N_pairs = 250. The realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and therefore reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements; consequently the paired-bootstrap CI and upper bound interpretation are the most informative outputs for practical decision-making.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: outcomes depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically checkable correctness but not emergent protocol-level properties. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and therefore generalization to heterogeneous production topologies or vendor heterogeneity is untested. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised here.

Operational implications (bounded). These results indicate that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single automated repair may be small; this finding is not evidence that validators or repairs are unnecessary in broader, production, adversarial, or cross-vendor contexts where validator scope or adversarial exposure differ.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. For N = 250 constrained synthetic intents produced by gpt-5-mini, initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and preregistration pointers: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Provider-call accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation + 1 repair) and stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} as recorded in the deterministic reconciliation artifact. The complete evidence bundle (execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, analysis CSVs, and reconciliation artifacts) is archived and referenced by the preregistration and master-prompt hashes above; file-level listings and per-artifact hashes are preserved in that archived bundle (not enumerated here). This Disclosure intentionally omits per-file paths and extensive file-level hashes from the main manuscript and instead provides the two immutable artifact references above (preregistration and master prompt) that enable deterministic traceability into the archived evidence bundle.

Deviation from preregistration: The preregistration specified multiple partitions including a planned sim-to-real (production-like) confirmatory contrast; that sim-to-real confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run. The executed confirmatory estimand reported here is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshot) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (live protocol dynamics or emergent cross-device interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
